quick_read.weather_md: **Weather:** 35°C high / 23°C low. Dry desert heat, spikes past 40°C (104°F). June is when Cairo heat becomes a health risk, not a discomfort.
quick_read.uv_md: **UV:** **UV 11+ — extreme.** Visible burn in 15 minutes mid-day. SPF 50+ won't fully save you if you spend a full afternoon outside.
quick_read.uv_advisory_md: *📎 Goose Investigation Bureau — sourcing UV from EPA + Cancer Research UK. UV 1–2 = no protection needed. UV 3+ = sunscreen + shade + hat + sunglasses. UV 8+ = limit midday sun. UV 11+ = stay out of midday sun entirely.*
quick_read.budget_hint_md: **Daily budget — $80 average.** Egypt is cheap on paper. Cost is not the constraint. The constraint is everything else.
quick_read.intro_md:
> **🚨 CLASSIFIED SIGNAL — DO NOT TRAVEL TO CAIRO IN THE NEXT 90 DAYS.**

> *Goose Investigation Bureau contacted embassies, locals, recent travelers, rights orgs, climate scientists, three taxi drivers, a hotel concierge, two journalists, and one baby mosquito we found in our office. Every channel returned the same signal. We're not in the business of telling you what to do. We're in the business of showing you what we found. So here it is — flat, no decoration.*

**The honest summary:**
- Two active government travel advisories
- Heat conditions that hospitalize tourists every June
- Documented harassment patterns toward female travelers
- Political environment where photographing the wrong thing is a real arrest risk
- Medical evacuation costs that exceed most travel insurance defaults
- Dust storms (declining but possible)
- An AQI that ranks among the worst in the world

**If your boss is sending you for a conference — push back.** Ask for remote attendance. The conference will happen next year, in a cooler month, when advisories are calmer.

**If your partner wants to go and you don't —** the next section is what to show them.
quick_read.do_now_md:
**Do now:**
- **Buy travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage — not optional.** Egyptian hospital quality outside private chains in Cairo is uneven; evac to Cyprus or Athens runs $50K–100K without insurance. Verify your policy excludes nothing for Egypt.
- **Register with your embassy.** US: STEP enrollment. UK: FCDO email register. Canada: ROCA. Takes 5 minutes. If anything happens, they know you're in-country.
- **Buy Grand Egyptian Museum tickets online NOW.** Walk-up sales are gone. Foreign adult ticket is around $29–30. Pick a morning slot. [src 5]
quick_read.restaurant_hook_md: **No Places to Eat list this brief — Michelin Guide doesn't currently publish for Egypt.** Eat at your hotel restaurant + 1 vetted spot (listed below in Worth Knowing). Don't experiment with street food on this trip.

happening.news_md:
### Government advisories — both are active

- **🇺🇸 US State Department — "Reconsider Travel."** This is one tier above "Exercise Increased Caution" — the State Department is explicitly telling you to weigh whether you should go at all. Sinai Peninsula and Western Desert: "Do Not Travel." Cairo + Giza: elevated risk. [src 1]
- **🇬🇧 UK FCDO — flagged, "heightened regional tension."** Tourist zones permitted but with warning. Embassy registration is recommended, not optional. [src 2]
- **🇦🇺 Australia Smartraveller — "Exercise a high degree of caution."** Same baseline as UK. [src 2]

### Political environment

Public protests are effectively banned under Sisi-era laws. Foreign tourists are not the target — but the rules apply to you anyway. Human Rights Watch's 2026 Egypt report documents continued mass detentions of activists, including foreign nationals tried in absentia. Do not photograph protests, do not discuss politics in cabs, do not sign anything someone hands you on the street. [src 3]

### Heat — the part most tourists underestimate

35°C average, 40°C+ spikes. Every June, foreign tourists are hospitalized at the Pyramids for heat stroke. Most are at the pyramids past 10am, in direct sun, without enough water. This is the cause of death — not anything dramatic, just the heat. [src 4]

### Dust + air quality

Khamsin (dust storms) are spring-peak, declining in June, but trend data shows increasing intensity year over year. Cairo's AQI sits at 150+ regularly through summer — that's "unhealthy for sensitive groups" on most days, "unhealthy for everyone" on bad days. If you have asthma, this trip becomes medically inadvisable, not just uncomfortable. [src 4]
happening.sports_md: - **Egyptian Premier League season ended May 20.** Zamalek SC won their 15th title. **No top-flight football in your window.** Friendlies and youth matches sometimes scheduled at smaller venues — check `english.ahram.org.eg` week-of if you're a football fan. [src 6]
happening.entertainment_md:
*Kept brief intentionally. This brief is not an itinerary builder.*

- **🏛️ Grand Egyptian Museum (Giza) — opened Nov 2025.** This is the one redeeming addition since 2025. World-class, AC-controlled, full Tutankhamun collection. 4-5 hours minimum. If you do nothing else, do this. [src 5]

brief.watch_md:
Kept brief intentionally. We're not building you an itinerary.

- **Giza Pyramids + Sphinx — dawn entry only — ~$30 entry.** Gates open 7am. Be there at 6:45. After 9:30am the heat is dangerous and the scams are heavier. Do not visit after lunch in June. Photo: camel viewpoint south of the plateau, before the buses arrive.
- **Grand Egyptian Museum — ~$29 adult.** Cannot overstate this. See above.

That's the list. We're not surfacing more.
brief.eat_md:
The Michelin Guide does not currently publish for Egypt. We have no vetted curated list to give you.

**Eat at your hotel restaurant. Full stop.** That is the recommendation.

If you wander beyond that, the GI risk on this trip is not abstract — every embassy briefing we read mentions traveler's diarrhea as the most common medical complaint. **Felfela in Downtown** is the one outside-the-hotel name that consistently comes up across recent traveler reports — go there once if you must, sit-down only, no street-food experiments on this trip.
brief.knowing_md:
> **If you ignore everything else in this brief, read this.**

- **Single women — harassment is documented and persistent.** Long sleeves + scarf cuts the volume significantly but does not eliminate it. Use the female-only metro carriage (front and back of every train). Stay in groups after dark. Do not share your live location publicly on social media. If a stranger holds a door open and won't move — walk through anyway, don't accept the "help."
- **Pyramid scams — all real, all documented.**
  - "Free camel photo" → $50 to dismount.
  - "The Sphinx is closed today, I'll show you a shortcut" → leads to a shop.
  - "I'm a Pyramid guard, give me your ticket" → not a guard.
  - **Polite firm "la, shukran" + walk + zero eye contact.**
- **Baksheesh (tipping) is constant.** Bathroom attendants, hotel staff, photo-takers, anyone holding a door. $1–2 each. Build a 10–15% cash buffer beyond your meal budget.
- **Medical evacuation insurance — not optional.** Hospital quality outside private chains is uneven; evac to Cyprus or Athens runs $50K–100K without coverage. Verify your policy excludes nothing for Egypt before you board.
- **Embassy registration — 5 minutes.** US: STEP. UK: FCDO. Canada: ROCA. Australia: Smartraveller. If something happens, they know you're in-country.
- **Private driver, not taxi.** Hotel-arranged, $40–60/day with English-speaking driver. Skips the negotiation tax and the gem-shop scams entirely. Worth every dollar.
- **Stay in Zamalek or Maadi.** Both are upscale, walkable, lower harassment. Avoid Downtown.
- **Tap water — bottled only. Brushing teeth too.** Ice from good restaurants is fine. Ice from street carts: skip.

budget_usd.notes: Mid = 4-star Zamalek hotel ($55), 3 meals at the hotel + 1 nice ($25), pyramid + museum tickets ($25). Don't skimp on the private driver. Don't skimp on the evacuation insurance.
